text:
ryan: Heads-up — saw a 2x slowdown on the 512 seqlen nightly perf run when enabling torch.compile + CUDA graphs. Only reproduces with batch sizes 1 and 2. :confused:

anya: Ugh. Is this the same job as the autotune CI? Which commit?

ryan: master@7f3b2e4. CI shows baseline (no compile/graphs) 55ms/token, with torch.compile+cudagraphs 110ms/token for seqlen=512, bs=1. seqlen=128 unaffected. Repro locally on A100.

leo: Can you paste the profiler output? Might be a kernel algo pick difference.

ryan: Dumping a quick nsys snippet — here's the hot kernel summary:```
# nsys summary (trimmed)
kernel: attention_forward, time_total: 18.2ms, calls: 1, chosen_algo: sm80_fused_attention_v3
kernel: matmul_mha_qk, time_total: 12.7ms, algo: cutlass_gemm_32x64, workspace: 0
kernel: softmax, time_total: 1.1ms
kernel: kv_cache_write, time_total: 4.8ms, calls: 1
```
Looks normal but the big difference is that with compile+cg we get an extra memcpy stage around kv_cache_write that shows as repeated writes.

morgan: Interesting — could be that CUDA-graph capture fused shapes and picked a kernel variant optimized for longer corridors, but our autotuner still thinks short-run is best. If compile hides dynamic dims, autotuner sampling may have seen only a different distribution.

leo: Hypothesis: torch.compile tracing + cudagraph capture makes the runtime present a single "canonical" shape (512) to the kernel selector, and our autotuner's sampling window happened during warmup with padded sequences ~1024, so selected a kernel that favors high throughput for longer sequences but has worse per-step latency for bs<=2.

anya: We should verify kernel fingerprint used by the autotuner vs runtime at request time. I can add a quick log to dump the chosen kernel id at runtime and in the autotune table.

cheng: Ran a narrower benchmark:
- baseline (no compile/graphs): bs1 seqlen512 -> 54.8ms/token
- torch.compile only: bs1 seqlen512 -> 58.1ms/token
- cudagraphs only: bs1 seqlen512 -> 56.0ms/token
- compile + cudagraphs: bs1 seqlen512 -> 111.3ms/token
So the combination is super non-linear. Also memory write throughput jumps in the combined case.

ryan: The weird memcpy is visible in nvprof:```
GPU memcpy HtoD: 0.9ms (expected)
device->device copy (internal): 9.6ms (extra)  # shows twice per step
```

morgan: Could be kv_cache layout changed by graph capture (inplace vs out-of-place) which forces a copy path. If kernel selection picked an algo that expects contiguous KV buffers but our capture altered alignment, runtime may insert alignment copies.

leo: Another angle — our autotuner uses a small batch of synthetic sequences for sampling. If torch.compile capture reorders ops (fusion), the post-fusion kernel candidates differ. Our offline autotune table stores based on pre-fusion op graph fingerprint, but the runtime uses fused fingerprint -> mismatch.

anya: Action item: add fingerprinting parity check between autotuner and runtime. If mismatch, skip cached entry and fallback to the safe low-latency kernel. I'll take this.

infra-bot: perf-ci nightly for job kvci-512 failed threshold: regression +98% on 2167890001. Details: https://ci.redwood/p/kvci-512/2167890001

cheng: Quick mitigation we tried locally: force-disable cudagraphs for seqlen>=256 when bs<=2. That restored baseline numbers (56ms/token). Not great but stops customer impact.

ryan: Good quick kill. We should avoid long-term special casing though.

morgan: For medium term: 1) fingerprint parity check, 2) autotuner sampling that runs under compiled/capture mode (i.e., sample after torch.compile/cudagraphs path), 3) improve KV buffer alignment invariants so capture doesn't change layout.

leo: Also log chosen kernel id + workspace size in telemetry for a while so we can correlate customer regressions.

anya: I'll open an issue and include a small repro harness. Plan: parity check + telemetry first patch. If parity mismatch, runtime should pick safe kernel and trigger background autotune under actual captured graph.

ryan: Can we add an abort-on-mismatch debug flag to CI so autotune/test jobs fail loudly? Would help detect this earlier.

morgan: Yep, add flag in autotuner harness. I'll update CI job.

cheng: I'll run a mini fleet run with the flag on a few spot VMs. Will post numbers.

leo: Thanks team. Assigning: anya -> parity check + issue; morgan -> CI flag update; cheng -> fleet run; ryan -> customer rollout block & temporary cudagraphs disable for small batches.

ryan: Opening the issue now and attaching prof traces. :rocket:

anya: thx. I'll start on a minimal parity-check patch and a test that simulates fused vs unfused fingerprints.

infra-bot: note: scheduled maintenance on build nodes at 03:00 UTC — might delay CI runs.

cheng: fleet run results (quick): with parity-check branch but no fallback, still replicates because autotune table used. With fallback -> safe kernel -> restores 56ms/token. Will iterate.

leo: Solid. Let's not forget to check HBM fragmentation patterns too; capture can change allocation ordering.

morgan: Good call. Add that to the issue.

ryan: OK closing the loop here for now. Follow-ups in the issue. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
